Re-merge divide parts split by geometry cleaning

Source: R/merge_bisected_divides.R
dot-merge_bisected_divides.Rd

mapshaper -clean, reached through hfutils::clean_gpkg_layer(), can bisect a narrow divide into disjoint parts. Casting that result to POLYGON turns the parts into separate rows sharing one divide_id, and keeping only one of them discards the rest. That silently destroys catchment area: across a national build it cost 886 km2, with every VPU still inside the 0.5% conservation tolerance, so nothing flagged it. It also strands the owning flowpath outside what remains of its catchment, which later reads as low coverage and gets the flowpath cleared and then deleted.

Usage

.merge_bisected_divides(d)

Arguments

d

Divides sf.

Value

A list with divides (the repaired layer), n_merged (divides whose parts were rejoined) and changed (whether anything was altered).

Details

A bisected divide is a cleaning artifact rather than two catchments: the parts were one divide before cleaning and belong to one flowpath after it. So normalize to MULTIPOLYGON, which is lossless and already the layer's type elsewhere, and union any rows sharing a divide_id back into one multipart feature.
